s1.syndrome_frame: Acute scrotal pain and swelling in a pediatric patient
salient_findings: Enlarged testis, epididymis, and infected appendages
Purulent foci on the surface of the sperm vessels
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with a five-day history of left scrotal soreness and oedema
No lower urinary tract symptoms
No major relevant medical or surgical history
Occult penis diagnosed based on penile characteristics
Other congenital anomalies of the genitourinary tract excluded based on imaging findings
Mild leukocytosis (18.5 × 10^9/L) on blood workup
Urine analysis was negative
Pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa, susceptible to ceftazidime and ofloxacin
Doppler ultrasonography showed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity
Follow-up sonography showed heterogeneous echotexture in the left testis and epididymis
MRI at 60 days showed no enhancement in T2, indicating disappearance of the left testis
Pathological examination showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage and fibrocystic-like tissue with inflammatory cell infiltration

shortlist.label: Epididymitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and laboratory tests showed mild leukocytosis and pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa

shortlist.label: Orchitis
shortlist.why_kept: Doppler ultrasonography revealed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity, consistent with orchitis

shortlist.label: Testicular appendage torsion
shortlist.why_kept: Pathological examination showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage, suggesting torsion of the appendage

shortlist.label: Epididymal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Pus culture isolated P. aeruginosa and patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, consistent with an epididymal abscess

shortlist.label: Scrotal cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and laboratory tests showed mild leukocytosis, consistent with scrotal cellulitis

raw.rationale: The patient presented with scrotal soreness and oedema, and imaging findings showed an enlarged left testis with heterogeneous echo pattern and enhanced vascularity, which is consistent with orchitis. The presence of mild leukocytosis and purulent foci on the surface of the sperm vessels also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Epididymitis
rejected.why: While epididymitis is a possible diagnosis, the imaging findings and laboratory results suggest that the testis is also involved, making orchitis a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Testicular appendage torsion
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not suggest torsion, and the presence of purulent foci and hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage is more consistent with orchitis.

rejected.label: Epididymal abscess
rejected.why: While an abscess is possible, the imaging findings and laboratory results suggest a more diffuse infection of the testis and epididymis, making orchitis a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Scrotal cellulitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings suggest a more localized infection of the testis and epididymis, rather than a diffuse infection of the scrotum.
